paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I won't pretend it isn't. God tells Ezekiel to confront the city with all her abominations, and the list reaches everybody: princes, priests, officials, prophets and everyday people (Ezekiel 22:6, 26-29). Notice the pattern, though. The people with the most power were hurting the people with the least, and the poor, the widow, the fatherless and the foreign resident paid for it (Ezekiel 22:7, 29). The sorrow under all of it is one line: "But Me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD" (Ezekiel 22:12).

Then God gives the furnace picture. The house of Israel has become dross, and He says He will gather them and melt them in the city (Ezekiel 22:18-22). I think that's a picture of how seriously God takes what He sees. He's not shrugging at it, and He's not looking away from the people who got hurt. When even the prophets say "This is what the Lord GOD says" when the LORD has not spoken, the baker learns to check every voice against the Word (Ezekiel 22:28).

And now the line that stays with me: "I searched for a man among them to repair the wall and stand in the gap before Me on behalf of the land, so that I should not destroy it. But I found no one" (Ezekiel 22:30). God was looking for someone to stand in that gap. Friend, that's why I keep my ovens ready and why I'm glad you're here in the Word. I bake to be ready, and I'm thankful every day that Jesus, the Lamb, stands in the gap for us (John 1:29).
